description: Known answers for the picotool sanity check (tools/toolchain.lock.md section 1.1, picotool row; CM plan section 9.2 table; TV due CDR). kat-target.elf is the image built from tools/tests/fixtures/rust/kat-target (its SHA-256 equals rust/known-answers.json target_build.elf_sha256). The UF2 known answer was computed independently of picotool, in Python, from the ELF: every PT_LOAD segment with a non-zero file size is placed at its physical address in 256-byte pages (unused bytes zero), one 512-byte UF2 block per page in address order (magics 0x0A324655, 0x9E5D5157, 0x0AB16F30; flags 0x00002000 family-id present; payload 256; family 0xE48BFF59), the block layout of the UF2 specification (github.com/microsoft/uf2; not in the reference corpus) with the rp2350_arm_s family id of RP2350 datasheet Table 454 in section 5.5 USB Mass Storage Interface (rustos docs/extracted/rp2350-datasheet.md). A wrong constant in the reconstruction would make it differ from picotool, so the byte-for-byte match checks both. The one image has one page at 0x10000000, so the UF2 is one block of 512 bytes. The program name is the string the fixture's binary-info entry carries (tools/tests/fixtures/rust/kat-target/src/main.rs).

uf2_convert.command: picotool uf2 convert kat-target.elf kat-target.uf2 --family rp2350-arm-s

info.command: picotool info -a kat-target.elf (and the same on kat-target.uf2)

verify.command: picotool load kat-target.uf2, then picotool verify kat-target.elf (pass) and picotool verify kat-target-1byte.elf, a copy with one byte changed (fail); needs the owner's Pico 2 in BOOTSEL mode
